why_selected: Opens the demo: counting one pitch in one voice by ear is hard for people too. No model answered correctly from the recording. The next item asks the same question as text; the last item of the demo asks it as a score image.
The same question as the previous item, now as ABC notation: all eight models are correct. For a person, reading ABC is possible but slow.

An interval in one voice, from a score image: a person reads the answer off the first notes of the tenor line. Half of the models were still wrong. The next item asks the same question from the recording.
The same question as the previous item, now from the recording: very hard to answer by ear.
Looks very simple: find the 18th note of one voice in the text. Yet only four of the eight models were correct.
An easy item: seven of the eight models answered correctly from ABC notation.
Hard from audio, easy from text: one model was correct from the recording. The next two items ask the same question as text and as a score image.
The same question as the previous item, as ABC notation: all eight models are correct.
The same question as the two previous items, as a score image, probably the easiest modality for a person. Half of the models were correct.
An example of the harmony questions: the relative major or minor of the piece's key, from the recording.
The same question as the previous item, as a score image, where the key signature can be read directly. Seven of the eight models were correct.
Reading a score image: counting one pitch in one voice. Half of the models were correct.
Reading a score image: seven of the eight models were correct.
A proportion question that is hard by ear: no model was correct from the recording. The next two items ask the same question as text and as a score image.
The same question as the previous item, as ABC notation: six of the eight models were correct.
The same question as the two previous items, as a score image, probably the easiest modality for a person. No model was correct.
Audio is not always the hardest: seven of the eight models named this note length correctly from the recording. The next item asks the same from the score image.
The same question as the previous item, as a score image: seven of the eight models were correct. Does this mean the models read note lengths from an image well?
Some items require counting far: the 52nd chord of the piece. Three of the eight models were correct.

The same question as items 1 and 2 at the start of the demo, as a score image. For most people this is the easiest of the three modalities; only one model was correct. The true count was not among the options here.
